headline: Re-running the engine is cheap, so offline re-scoring is a screening tool, not the main loop. Measured on the 4,383,562-tick month 2026-11, 2 threads, steady state: 0.19 s (shipped alert x7.5) and 0.03 s (calibrated x30) per replay; results/queue.log gives 316 full-feed replays in 531 s and 48 in 49 s, i.e. about 1.0 to 1.7 s per replay of all 62,732,047 ticks on 4 cores. Idle skipping via Sim._cand (sim.py:48-59) must stay: candidate ticks are 0.53% (x30) to 20.0% (x7.5) of ticks, yet the engine evaluates the direction state (C_DECISIONS, engine.py:1049) on 1.80M ticks (x30), 20.69M (x7.5, 33% of ticks) and 42.09M (x3), summed over the 9 months. Offline re-scoring only pays above roughly 1e5 input sets.

Order flow touches the engine in exactly two ways. (a) One read per direction evaluation: EA BuildDirectionState 2339-2342, ScoreOrderFlow 2463-2493, AddFlowVote 2556-2569. (b) A per-order label ':FA'/':FD' (EA ShortComment 3140-3141) that four exit branches read later (EA 11218-11262 stop-flow danger close, 10900-10906 V40 pre-speed shield, 10921-10927 FOLM danger loss, 10948-10953 immediate-by-flow) plus MarketEntryAllowedByFlow (2770-2789), BlockStrongFlowAgainst (2748) and the scenario keys BFNF/FLXQ/BFNO/BFA (3159-3186). The change is four per-chunk arrays (fl_ix int32[n_ticks], fl_t int64, fl_ok uint8, fl_v float64[n,3]), about 25 lines at decision time and one label array per order table; empty arrays or UseOrderFlow=false means neutral. Because flow is read only on ticks the engine already processes, idle skipping is untouched. Scratch prototype: neutral-flow output is bit-identical to the current engine (all 18 trade columns, all 21 counters) for 5 presets on 2026-11.

The 11 flow inputs missing from engine.NAMES must be added: UseOrderFlow, MaxFlowAgeMs, MinFlowImbalance, FlowComponentScore, BlockStrongFlowAgainst, FlowDisagreeMakesDefenseImmediate, FOLMFlowDisagreeDangerLossPoints, UseStopFlowDisagreeDangerClose, StopFlowDisagreeDangerLossPoints, StopFlowDisagreeDangerMinHoldMs, StopFlowDisagreeDangerNeedsOppositePressure (results/inputs_classification.csv lists them as 'no effect in the tester'). Live semantics from the EA: globals XPW_XAU_OK / HEARTBEAT / FORCE_IMB / NEAR_IMB / BOOK_IMB; fresh iff OK >= 0.5 and GetTickCount64 - HEARTBEAT <= MaxFlowAgeMs (4000); every one of the 3 values with |v| >= MinFlowImbalance (5.0) adds FlowComponentScore (1.0) to its side; flowDir needs 2 same-sign votes. The feed's scale, cadence and predictive content are NOT in the package and could not be determined. The EA's own live logs are the only source: SpeedAlertRouter_XAUUSD_scenario_v48_3.csv (LogDecision, EA 13101-13151: flow_fresh, flow_dir, force_imb, near_imb, book_imb, buy_score, sell_score, speed_dir, speed_points, body_dir, body_pts, upper_wick, lower_wick, micro_dir, spread_stable, follow21, follow37, opposite_pressure, snapback, mfe, mae) and SAR_OrderFlowDecision_v2.csv (time_msc). Reuse those column names in the engine log so live and replay rows join. Free side data: Dukascopy top-of-book sizes exist in data/hf parquet (bid_volume, ask_volume) and in the raw bi5 (fetch_dukascopy.py:31 av/bv) but are dropped by fetch_hf_ticks.py:57 and the npz store; a BOOK_IMB proxy at best.

Real-account facts to fit and validate the synthetic feed against, re-derived from results/real/real_trades_sar.csv: 2,584 trades; labels FA 1,609 (62%), FD 409 (16%), none 566 (22%); FOLM market route 1,911 trades (74%), of which 1,527 FA; profit factor by label 0.80 / 0.92 / 0.85, so flow agreed with the trades that did worst. None of the four flow-dependent exit branches ever fired (real exits: SL 1,370, speed exit 785, FOLM_SM_EARLY 102, TP 90, V40 retest shield 80, FOLM_WARN24 73, other 56, V40_FLXQ_SS 28; the replay has 0 SA_PRE_SPEED_DEFENSE exits in 9,282 trades). Implement those branches with forced-state unit tests but spend no calibration effort on them; what flow really changes is routing (market vs stop) and the score.

The engine re-evaluates direction on every tick of an alert window and the first passing tick enters, so the direction logic is a first-passage detector: per-tick noise in a flow series is a multiple-comparison lottery. A toy 1 Hz momentum-coupled series took the shipped preset from 545 to 1,006 trades in 2026-11 (labels FA 414 / FD 45 / none 547). The series must be piecewise constant between published updates (period_ms >= 250, default 1000), carry its own heartbeat and OK flags so MaxFlowAgeMs stays a calibratable input, and be generated on the replay clock without look-ahead. Cost, measured: 58-72 ns/tick and 10.5-10.8 B/tick at 1 Hz (about 0.67 GB for the whole feed), 144 ns/tick and 30-31 B/tick at 4 Hz (about 1.9 GB), so build per chunk and keep at most two series cached.

Decision log = one row per C_DECISIONS increment (engine.py:1049) plus one row per entry-hold pass. Prototype results on 2026-11: rows == C_DECISIONS exactly; the stage histogram equals the engine counters for all 14 stages; 545/545 trades link to their row through a new signal_ms; trades are bit-identical with logging on or off; byte-identical logs for 1, 2 and 3 worker threads. Cost 4.2 us per row (1.99 s vs 0.19 s per month, about 10x a plain replay) and 288 B per row (58 int32 + 14 float32). Full-feed volumes at 288 B/row: 1.80M rows = 0.52 GB at x30, 20.69M rows = 5.96 GB at x7.5, so write per chunk and never hold the log. Exactness rule: store tick indices into the feed (M1 bar open/high/low, micro-break and opposite-pressure extremes, prior-drift and burst reference ticks, alert start, MFE/MAE extremes) and binary-exact flow values (quantise synthetic imbalances to 1/8), never float32 copies of float64 values that are later compared with an input, so ties behave as in the engine.

Offline re-scoring is exact for score, winner, router action, scenario key, flow label and FlashGold gate verdict, but only on rows the base run evaluated, and alert-level features are path state. Measured: re-scoring winner/action/scenario/flow label from a theta0 log equals the engine at theta' on 100% of shared rows for 15 input variants (shared 443,407 to 935,316 rows each; 936,868 at theta0); the gate verdict is exact for 6 gate-input variants. But a theta0 log contains only 33.8% to 99.6% of the rows a variant evaluates (34% for MinDirectionScore 5, 63% for MaxSpreadPoints 12), and a never-resolving shadow log covers 89-99% of ticks but only 9-45% of (tick, alert start, direction), because after every FlashGold / prior-60 / burst / hold block the engine re-alerts with a new start tick. Recommended inner loop for direction calibration: an X_SignalOnly engine replay (entry chain only, placement written as a signal row, no orders or positions). Its placement list equals a full replay with caps, lockout and speed-exit alert resets switched off exactly (2,532/2,532 and 465/465 on 2026-11). The state-dependent remainder (cap_skip 497 vs placed 1,735 and lockout_skip 952 for the shipped preset; 87 vs 312 and 88 for the calibrated one; hold_failed_bar blocks 77% of would-be hold arms at x7.5 and 44% at x30) belongs to a full-replay confirmation of the shortlist.

Forward outcomes belong in a separate post-pass kernel that reuses the engine's broker arithmetic (engine.py:410-425 stop-loss/take-profit fills, 488-506 delayed market fill, 1381-1389 SL/TP from the decision-tick quote). For BOTH sides it returns the signed mid move at 9 horizons (0.5 to 60 s), MFE/MAE in 4 windows and 6 SL/TP brackets (90/180, 90/600, 130/600, 200/600, 60/180, 80/160) from a market entry with 150 ms delay, 10 point snap and stop-loss slip factor 1.5. Validated against the engine in pure-bracket mode (EA-side exits off): 3,603/3,603 market trades identical in points and exit reason, max difference 0.0000. Cost 8.5 us per row single thread (12.0 s for 1.40M rows), 244 B per row.

Engineering constraints: numba compile grows from about 31 s to 44 s (cache=True; any signature or dtype change recompiles). run_chunk has exactly two callers (sim.py:85, selftest.py:133). Sim._idx/_cand are called from the worker threads (sim.py:70-91) and _cand clears its dict above 400 entries (sim.py:51-52), a latent KeyError race: build all caches in the calling thread before the pool (done in the prototype). Output buffers truncate silently at 20,000 trades per chunk (sim.py:72) and 12 position/order slots (MAXP/MAXO, engine.py:149-150), so log capacity overflow must be asserted via a counter. Per-month feeds change results slightly (9,241 vs 9,282 shipped-preset trades, because weekly chunks are cut at month ends): confirm on the whole feed, use per-month feeds only to stay inside 16 GB while logging. Scratch evidence: prototype diffs and 16 test scripts (adapted to read PROTO_TOOLS: see prototypes/README.md) are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-master/8b335e1d-7919-5695-aa16-fdeb3605b836/scratchpad/prompt_work/engine-plan/ (prototype_engine.diff +414/-49 lines, prototype_sim.diff +30/-8, prototype_params.diff +1/-1); the repo was not written by me. git status in the repo now shows REPORT.md, REPORT.template.md and tools/make_report.py modified at 16:08, by another actor.

flow_arrays_design:
Per chunk (one weekly chunk of the Feed, indexed like feed.t[a:b]), four arrays, all C-contiguous and writable (read-only or mmap arrays make numba compile a second specialisation): fl_ix int32[n_ticks] = index of the last published update at or before tick i (-1 = none yet; this is the alignment array, O(1) lookup, same pattern as idxL), fl_t int64[nu] = heartbeat / publication time in feed ms (strictly increasing), fl_ok uint8[nu] = the feed's OK flag, fl_v float64[nu,3] = FORCE_IMB, NEAR_IMB, BOOK_IMB as published (synthetic values quantised to 1/8 so float32 copies in the log and threshold ties are exact). Neutral flow = empty arrays (shapes (0,), (0,), (0,), (0,3)) or UseOrderFlow = 0. Freshness model for MaxFlowAgeMs: at decision tick i, k = fl_ix[i]; fresh = k >= 0 and fl_ok[k] != 0 and (T[i] - fl_t[k]) <= MaxFlowAgeMs. Outages are modelled by gaps in fl_t or fl_ok = 0, so the same code path gives 'stale'. Publication lag is modelled by shifting fl_t later than the information time, never earlier. The engine reads the series only at the direction evaluation (engine.py:1113) and at no other tick, and then carries the label fl_lab = +1 (FA) / -1 (FD) / 0 on the pending, market and position tables; the entry-hold path restores the label stored at the arm tick (hold_fl).

Build and cache: tools/flowsim.py with spec = {model: 'neutral'|'tape'|'lead'|'replay', period_ms: 1000, lag_ms: 0, seed, quant: 0.125, scales / information coefficient, dropout: {p_outage, mean_ms}} (JSON-able; flow_key(spec) mirrors flashgold.fg_key). 'tape' = contemporaneous series from the last 1-3 s of mid moves plus noise; 'lead' = adds a controlled share of FUTURE return (look-ahead by construction, label results as upper bounds); 'replay' = piecewise-constant series from the owner's live CSV samples. FlowSeries(feed, spec).chunk(c) builds lazily with np.random.default_rng([seed, chunk_start_ms]) (deterministic, independent of thread order), vectorised over the update grid: grid = np.arange(t0, t_end+1, period); j = np.searchsorted(t, grid, 'right') - 1; ret = (mid[j] - mid[j3]) / 0.01 ...; values = np.round(v * 8) / 8; fl_ix = (np.searchsorted(grid, t, 'right') - 1).astype(np.int32). Sim keeps a dict of at most 2 FlowSeries keyed by flow_key (like fg_cache at sim.py:35) and Sim.run prebuilds every chunk in the calling thread before pool.map; optional disk cache in data/cache/ (already in .gitignore) as npz keyed by hash(spec, feed identity). Prototype numbers: 1 Hz = 58-72 ns/tick and 10.5-10.8 B/tick (0.54 s and 99 MB for the 9.24M-tick month 2026-03), 4 Hz = 144 ns/tick and 30-31 B/tick.

decision_log_design:
Where: a row is opened at engine.py:1049 (cnt[C_DECISIONS] += 1) and finished when the same iteration ends (deferred flush at the loop top, so each of the 14 early exits only sets lg_stage). A second row (kind 1) is opened when an armed entry hold is evaluated (engine.py:1043-1046) and carries stage, hold_move, FlashGold verdict at the pass tick and a link LI_ARMROW to the arm row. Rows exist only on ticks the engine really evaluates (idle skipping intact).

Record (prototype: 58 int32 + 14 float32 = 288 B; real version also adds the alert tick, MFE/MAE extreme indices and a per-second float64 CP table; names mirror the EA's SpeedAlertRouter_XAUUSD_scenario_v48_3.csv so live and replay rows can be joined): identity (chunk, tick index, ms offset, alert episode id, kind); alert (speed_dir, speed_pts, alert start tick -> speed_start_mid, alert tick); score components (buy_score, sell_score, speed_dir, body_dir, micro_dir, flow votes vb/vs, spread via the feed at the tick); candle (tick indices of bar open / high / low -> body, up_wick, lo_wick); micro-break (index of highest/lowest mid for L = 2,5,10,20,30,60 s); flow (fl_k, fresh, flow_dir, FORCE/NEAR/BOOK as float32); follow flags and MFE/MAE since the alert start; opposite pressure and snapback inputs (window start, lowest and highest mid for W = 2,3,5,10 s; flag bits); router outputs (action, scenario key, flow label, exhaustion/continuation/wick/follow flag bits); FlashGold (z verdict, filter bar index, so the scorer re-evaluates gate inputs with the same _fg_z kernel); continuation-filter stats (count60, median gap, range60, range300, median spread, complete flags); prior-60 drift as the reference tick for 15/30/60/120 min; burst gate reference tick; engine state (npos, npend, nmk, lockout flag); stage code (ST_MIXED, ST_SPREAD, ST_FLOWBLK, ST_BODYAG, ST_TRADESIDE, ST_FGBLOCK, ST_HOLDBAR, ST_HOLDARM, ST_HOLDFAIL, ST_PRIOR60, ST_BURST, ST_CAP, ST_CPBLOCK, ST_PLACED). Storage: one npz/npy pair per chunk written by the worker, never accumulated; optional X_LogMinGapMs decimation applies only to ST_MIXED rows (they are 90% of rows at x7.5: 1,265,014 of 1,404,279 in 2026-11; 71% at x30).

Forward outcomes (tools/declog.py, separate post-pass, both sides, parallel over chunks): input = row tick indices; horizons 0.5,1,2,3,5,10,20,30,60 s: signed mid move (zero-order hold, NaN past the chunk end); MFE and MAE of the signed mid move in 5,10,30,60 s; brackets (SL,TP) in {90/180, 90/600, 130/600, 200/600, 60/180, 80/160}: market entry on the first tick >= t + 150 ms at ask (buy) / bid (sell) (engine.py:488-506), SL/TP from the quote of the DECISION tick rounded to 0.01 (1381-1389), position checked from the tick after the fill, stop loss fills at its level when the touch is within 10 points else slips floor(gap/PT*1.5 + 0.5)*PT, take profit fills at the market, still open at hmax (300 s) closed at the market (reason HORIZON). Output per row and side: points net, reason, ms to exit. Run it for slip factors 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0 (the REPORT shows the calibrated profit factor moving 1.25 / 1.15 / 1.06 with it). A stop-order-entry variant (StopEntryDistancePoints, PendingExpirySeconds) is an optional extension and NOT validated. Placed trades get full-replay outcomes from the normal trade list; rows that were not traded only get the kernel.

Signal-only mode (X_SignalOnly) is the cheap direction-calibration inner loop: same chain, placement = a signal row with reason R_SIGNAL and no order; combine with the forward kernel on the signal ticks only.

Exact (measured on 2026-11 with a toy flow series, prototype rescore.py): re-scoring SpreadStableScore, SpeedDirectionScore, MaxSpreadPoints, MinCandleBodyPoints, CandleBodyScore, MicroBreakLookbackSeconds (grid 2,5,10,20,30,60 s), MicroBreakBufferPoints, MicroBreakScore, MinFlowImbalance, FlowComponentScore, MaxFlowAgeMs, MinDirectionScore, MinScoreEdge, OppositePressureSeconds (grid 2,3,5,10 s), OppositePressurePoints, RetestFailPoints, MarketFollow21/37 points and seconds, EntryRouterMode, WeakFlowMarket*, DowngradeNeutralSellMarketToStop and BlockStrongFlowAgainst from a theta0 log reproduces the engine's winner, action, scenario key and flow label on 100% of rows shared with the engine run at theta' (15 variants, 443,407 to 935,316 shared rows each). FlashGold gate-only inputs (FG_InpBandAtr, FG_InpAgainst, FG_InpAllowBuy/Sell, FG_InpLast/Seconds/Minutes/Bars) re-score exactly by calling _fg_z on the logged tick (6 variants, up to 1,404,279 rows). Prior-60 sign test, burst gate and continuation-filter checks are exact from the logged reference ticks / per-second statistics. FilterSeries-building inputs (FG_InpBurstAtr, EntryDistAtr, FG_InpTf, parent/zone settings, FG_Resolution) need a new FilterSeries (cached by fg_key), not a new log.

Not exact, because state depends on earlier decisions: (1) alert inputs (MaxTrailingMultiplier, MinSpeedAlertPoints, SpeedLookbackSeconds, SpeedAlertHoldSeconds) change which ticks exist: regenerate the log per alert setting (outer loop, a few settings). (2) Censoring: a log only holds the ticks its own run evaluated; a variant evaluates ticks the base run never reached (shared fraction 33.8% to 99.6%). (3) Alert-level features (start tick, follow21/37, MFE/MAE, snapback) are path state: the engine restarts the alert with a fresh start after every FlashGold/prior-60/burst/hold block, so a never-resolving shadow log covers 89-99% of ticks but only 9-45% of (tick, alert start, direction). (4) Entry-hold automaton incl. hold_failed_bar (blocks 77% of would-be arms at x7.5, 44% at x30 in 2026-11), lockout after 3 defensive closes, scenario caps and one-order-per-scenario (cap_skip is 22% of would-place events: 497/(1,735+497) shipped, 87/(312+87) calibrated), CancelOldPendings, speed-exit alert resets.

Honest protocol: (a) use the log for analysis (information value of each component, calibration of weights/thresholds as a classifier on forward outcomes) and for screening only near theta0 where coverage is above ~88%; (b) for search use X_SignalOnly replays (0.2 to 1.7 s per full-feed theta on 4 cores; identical placements to a full replay without caps/lockout/speed-exit coupling), then forward outcomes on the signals; (c) confirm every shortlisted theta in the full replay and report both numbers plus the rank correlation between offline score and full-replay profit factor over a random sample of at least 50 thetas; do not trust the offline ranking if that correlation is low; (d) an optional union-window tick table (every tick inside any potential alert window: 2.96M ticks at x30 = 4.7% of ticks, 7.49M at x20, 13.09M at x15, 33.68M at x7.5 = 53.7%) plus an offline automaton replicating engine.py:1022-1437 without positions would make counterfactual re-scoring complete, but it duplicates the state machine and is only worth building if signal-only replays are too slow for the search space.
performance_estimate: All timings measured on the scratch prototype (2 threads, machine shared). Plain replay of 2026-11 (4,383,562 ticks, 2 chunks): shipped alert x7.5 0.191 s, toy 1 Hz flow 0.216 s (+13%, because trades roughly double), signal-only 0.186 s; calibrated alert x30 0.028 s neutral, 0.023 s with flow, 0.014 s signal-only. Whole feed: results/queue.log implies about 1.0 to 1.7 s per replay on 4 cores; per-month sums of my runs were 3.1 s (x7.5) and 0.4 s (x30) at 2 threads. Logging run: 1.99 s for 950,332 rows (x7.5, toy flow) = 4.2 us per row, 0.114 s for 35,584 rows (x30); first call after an engine edit 44 s (compile) instead of 31 s. Micro-benchmarks per call: micro-grid 0.6 us, opposite-pressure grid 0.16 us, prior drift (4 horizons) 0.7 us, _cp_stats 9.1 us (once per distinct second), 1 s lookback 24 ns. Rows over all 9 months: C_DECISIONS 1.80M (x30), 20.69M (x7.5), 42.09M (x3); union of potential alert windows 2.96M (x30), 7.49M (x20), 13.09M (x15), 33.68M (x7.5), 55.83M (x3) ticks. Disk/memory at 288 B per log row plus 244 B per forward-outcome row: x30 = 0.52 GB + 0.44 GB; x7.5 = 5.96 GB + 5.05 GB; stream per chunk, so peak RAM is about 4 x (rows per chunk x 532 B) = roughly 1 to 2 GB with 4 workers on top of the 7 GB feed (use per-month feeds when logging at x7.5). Forward kernel 8.5 us per row single thread (12.0 s for 1.40M rows); x30 whole feed about 15 s single / 4 s on 4 threads, x7.5 about 176 s single / 45 s on 4 threads. Log generation x7.5 whole feed about 20-30 s plus disk. Flow series: 4 s and 0.67 GB for the whole feed at 1 Hz, 9 s and 1.9 GB at 4 Hz. Thread safety: workers own their out/cnt/lgi/lgf and the helper functions are nogil; shared caches (_idx, _cand, flow, fg) must be built before the pool; verified byte-identical logs and trades for 1, 2 and 3 workers.
risks: The synthetic feed is not the real feed: scale, cadence and predictive content are unknown, and the real labels (FA agrees with the worse trades: PF 0.80 vs 0.92) suggest flow is contemporaneous with the burst rather than predictive. Treat results as sensitivity analysis over an information coefficient, fit the generator to the live CSV logs (marginals, update cadence, freshness duty cycle, FA/FD/none 62/16/22%, FA share of FOLM 80%), and label any 'lead' model as an upper bound.

First-passage lottery: per-tick evaluation inside 20 s windows multiplies any noise (toy series: 545 -> 1,006 trades). The Dukascopy-based replay has 4.5 ticks/s on average and 7.8 ticks/s at candidate ticks, which need not match the broker's evaluations per window; entry counts and first-pass timing will not transfer 1:1 to live.

Look-ahead leakage: features must only use ticks <= i and flow published at or before the tick; forward outcomes are labels only. Add a truncation test (cut the feed after tick i and require identical logged features at row i).

Engine/scorer drift: two implementations of the same scoring. Mitigate with shared njit kernels (_fg_z and the log helpers) and the master parity test (re-score at theta0 and at theta' equals engine on 100% of shared rows). Never store float32 copies of values later compared with inputs (mfe/mae and CP stats are float32 in the prototype and matched on 15 variants, but ties are a latent risk: store indices or float64).
Censoring and path state (see limits): using a theta0 log to rank distant thetas is biased; only signal-only replays or full replays are exact for search.

Overfitting and multiple testing: a search over 1e5 to 1e7 input sets on about 1,200-trade samples; the REPORT already found rank correlation 0.06 between calibration and validation profit factor of neighbouring sets and a hold-out that is no longer clean. Forward-outcome metrics over thousands of signals are less noisy than trade profit factor but need nested validation and a count of effective trials.

Fill-model dependence: forward labels inherit the 150 ms delay, 10 point snap and stop-loss slip factor 1.5 (fitted on one month of real fills); compute labels for factors 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0 and require the ranking to be stable.

Numba: any run_chunk signature, dtype or readonly change recompiles (about 44 s); keep arrays int32/int64/uint8/float64 C-contiguous and writable; a variable first assigned inside a branch must be initialised before it (fl_lab, sig_ms); silent truncation limits (20,000 trades per chunk at sim.py:72, MAXP/MAXO = 12) need assertions, plus log_rows_dropped == 0.
Latent Sim._cand race (sim.py:48-59 called from worker threads, clear() above 400 entries): fix when adding the flow cache.
Per-month feeds cut weekly chunks (9,241 vs 9,282 shipped-preset trades); never mix per-month and whole-feed numbers in one comparison.

The four flow-dependent exits are unvalidated (no real occurrences, rare in replay); implement exactly from EA 10888-10990 and 11218-11262 with forced-state unit tests, and do not let them drive calibration.

Memory: whole feed 7 GB + idx cache 0.5 GB per lookback + flow 0.67 to 1.9 GB + log chunks; the union table at x7.5 would be 9.7 GB on disk; run_all.sh's rule of one feed-loading process at a time must stay.
